title: Reverse Hack Squat
summary: A hack squat done facing the pad with your hips pushed back. It shifts the work from the quads toward the glutes and hamstrings.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine); weight plates.

muscles.why: Library rating 0.9 for glutes (main mover): each working set adds 0.9 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.75 for quads (main mover): each working set adds 0.75 of a set to the weekly quads total.
Library rating 0.5 for adductors (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly adductors total.
Library rating 0.4 for hamstrings (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly hamstrings total.
Library rating 0.2 for lower back: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly lower back total.

setup.text: Face the machine with your chest on the back pad and your shoulders under the pads.
Push your hips back and squat down until your hips are deeply flexed.
Drive back up through your heels.

form_cues.cue: Push the hips back as you lower
Let your hips travel back, not just down.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds two or three ramp-up sets at rising loads before the first working set, unless that load is very light.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 6-10 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less stretch emphasis, More quad-focused, One side at a time.

notes: Ratings, swap attributes and cues are the library model (modeled). An authored page will replace this one.
